Items.Authors: Zhengjiang Zhang, Huatao Zhang, Yanbing Chen, Tong Zhou, Kai Zhang, Mingda Jiang, Zhen Tang
Items.Title: On-site integration and commissioning of a high-resolution echelle spectrograph for the 1.2m astronomical telescope of Sun Yat-Sen University
Items.Abstract: The astronomical high dispersion spectrograph for the 1.2-meter astronomical telescope is a fiber-fed, high-resolution echelle spectrograph located at the astronomical station of Zhuhai campus of Sun Yat-Sen University. It is fed by the Cassegrain focus via a 25-meter-long, 2.7’’ optical fiber. The spectrograph provides spectral resolution higher than 30000 over the wavelength range of 400-900nm. It enables the science team to do frontier researches and education in astronomical fields such as chemical element abundance measurement, stellar formation and evolution. This paper mainly describes the spectrograph alignment and the commissioning performance. We adopted a method of combining autocollimation with Knife-Edge test to intuitively and precisely align the optical axis of each optical component, and improve working efficiency. With the commissioning observations, the instrumental performance has been further optimized and met the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Sergio D'Orsi, Salvatore Savarese, Pietro Schipani, Laurent Marty, Giulio Capasso, Ricardo Zanmar Sánchez, Kalyan Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Andrea Baruffolo, Davide Ricci, Bernardo Salasnich, Paolo D'Avanzo, Sergio Campana, Riccardo Claudi, David Young, Marco Landoni, Matteo Munari, Stephen Smartt, Matteo Genoni, Fabrizio Vitali, Salvatore Scuderi, Rosario Cosentino, Frédéric Dérie, Markus Schoeller, Armin Silber, Ivo Saviane, Emanuela Pompei, Derek Ives, Antonio Miccichè, Gaetano Nicotra, Eugenio Martinetti, Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Adam Rubin, Marco Riva, Michael Rappaport, Giuliano Pignata, Luigi Lessio, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Ofir Hershko, Francesco D'Alessio, Anna Brucalassi, Alex Bichkovsky, Sagi Ben-Ami, José Antonio Araiza-Durán, Maximilian Stritzinger, Seppo Mattila, Avishay Gal-Yam, Iair Arcavi, Massimo Della Valle, Enrico Cappellaro, Antonio Sulich, Jani Achrén, Marcos Hernandez Diaz, Jari Kotilainen, Gianluca Li Causi, Hector Pérez Ventura
Items.Title: On-site integration and validation of the SOXS control electronics at ESO-NTT
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) instrument is a dual-arm, wide-band spectrograph designed to provide rapid and flexible follow-up observations of transient phenomena with the ESO NTT.  After successfully completing its Preliminary Acceptance in Europe at the end of 2024, the instrument was shipped to the ESO La Silla Observatory.  This paper presents the on-site integration and validation of the SOXS control electronics.  We describe the tests performed at the telescope, including hardware integration, verification of network and software interfaces, functional checks of the motion and thermal control systems, and communication tests with the instrument control software.  Particular emphasis is placed on the assessment of timing stability, electromagnetic compatibility within the telescope environment, and system robustness under operational constraints such as temperature variations and safety interlocks, highlighting lessons learned that guided the optimization of the system.

Items.Authors: Rasjied Sloot, Rudy Wijnands, Steven Bloemen, Hans Ellermeijer, Alexander Hoogerbrug, Rik ter Horst
Items.Title: On-sky commissioning and technical performance of Proto-NUX at Pic du Midi
Items.Abstract: The Near-Ultraviolet eXplorer (NUX) is a proposed ground-based observing facility designed to expand near-ultraviolet (NUV) astronomy by enabling observations in the 300--350 nm range from Earth. To validate this concept, a single-telescope prototype, Proto-NUX, was commissioned at the Pic du Midi Observatory in the French Pyrenees during its first high-altitude observing campaign in March 2026. The campaign tested deployment, remote operation, calibration, detector performance, image quality, tracking, and simultaneous optical monitoring under realistic observing conditions. In particular, the delivered NUV point-spread function was broader than expected, likely due to residual collimation, chromatic effects, and internal reflections. The detector dark current contributed significantly to the noise budget. We discuss limitations and key improvements for future Proto-NUX campaigns and the NUX system.

Items.Authors: Aditi Desai, Stephanie E. Sallum, Andrew J. Skemer
Items.Title: On-sky demonstration of speckle noise removal using the SCALES medium-spectral-resolution mode
Items.Abstract: The Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) is a 2-5 micron high-contrast lenslet-based integral field spectrograph (IFS) designed to detect and characterize exoplanets. The SCALES medium-resolution mode comprises a lenslet subarray with a 0.34 x 0.36 arcsecond field of view (FOV) and an image slicer, allowing for measurements of molecular abundances and disequilibrium chemistry in giant exoplanet atmospheres at increased spectral resolution. This mode uses a piezo-electric mirror to offset the FOV from the star to the planet. We use SCALES commissioning data to perform tests on speckle noise removal software designed specifically for observations this mode, employing angular and spectral differential imaging to mitigate stellar, atmospheric, and instrumental noise effects. We demonstrate the achievable contrast for the medium-resolution mode and use the results to estimate our ability to recover planet signals and characterize exoplanet atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Roland Winkler, Weijia Sun, Daniel Sablowski, Thomas Liebner, Ole Streicher, Steffen Frey, Ingo Stilz, Alexander Pramskiy, Scott Smedley, Thomas Szeifert, Diogo Rio Fernandes, Gerard Zins
Items.Title: On-sky fibre-target-alignment of the 4MOST instrument: calibration and performance
Items.Abstract: The 4-metre Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope (4MOST) is a new wide-field, fibre-fed spectroscopic survey facility for the VISTA telescope at ESO’s Paranal Observatory. The instrument enables the simultaneous acquisition of 2436 spectra across a 4.2 deg² field of view, using a tilting spine fibre positioner feeding three dedicated spectrographs. In this paper, we describe the final calibration process, and performance verification of the Fibre-Target-Alignment (FTA) for 4MOST on the VISTA telescope. We show how reach a final positioning performance of approximately 16u m / 0.27 arc sec relative to targets on sky.

Items.Authors: Jens-Kristian Krogager, Johan Richard, Florence Laurent, Mark Cunningham
Items.Title: On-sky performance of 4MOST low resolution spectrographs
Items.Abstract: 4MOST, the 4m Multi Object Spectroscopic Telescope, is an optical, fibre-fed, MOS facility for the VISTA telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. Its main science drivers are in the fields of galactic archeology, high-energy physics, galaxy evolution and cosmology. 4MOST recently received its first light in October 2025 and is starting operations in 2026. Here we present the results of on-sky tests obtained on the two low-resolution spectrographs (1624 fibres, three arms, 370-950 nm, R > 4000) which were constructed under the responsibility of CRAL. We present our efforts to characterize the instrument focus after installation on the telescope as well as an on-sky validation of performance in terms of spectral resolution, cross-talk, line-spread function and stability.

Items.Authors: Mayra Gutierrez, Maïssa Salama, Mahawa Cissé, Steph Sallum, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Charlotte Guthery, Antonin Bouchez, Katherine de Kleer
Items.Title: On-sky science verification of Keck Observatory's HAKA adaptive optics upgrade
Items.Abstract: Early in 2026, Keck Observatory will upgrade its adaptive optics system to feature a 2844-actuator deformable mirror as part of the High-Order All-Sky Keck Adaptive Optics project (HAKA). To characterize HAKA’s on-sky performance, we evaluate its K-band Strehl ratio as a function of guide-star magnitude using NIRC2, and compare these results to Strehl ratios obtained with the previous 349-actuator system. We further evaluate HAKA’s performance through z-band observations of Solar System objects and by measuring achievable contrast curves with NIRC2. Since Keck Observatory will also be integrating the Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) in 2026, we will repeat these on-sky HAKA observations with SCALES, as available. Together, these measurements will provide the first comprehensive on-sky assessment of HAKA’s science capabilities and inform the planetary science and high-contrast exoplanet imaging programs enabled by the upgraded Keck AO system.

Items.Authors: William O'Brien, Stuart Jeffries, Fabien Baron, Douglas Hope, Dmitriy Shcherbik
Items.Title: On-sky speckle spectral recovery
Items.Abstract: Detailed characterization of astronomical objects requires spatial and spectral information. Recent work shows that high-spatial, low-spectral resolution data can be recovered from short-exposure (“speckle”) broadband (δλ/λ ∼ 100%) images. We demonstrate that diffraction, turbulence, and dispersion—which normally cause image smear—can instead be used to extract 3D (x, y, λ) information from a time series of broadband speckle frames.    A major advantage of this method is its simple instrumentation: a wavefront sensor and a fast camera. A full model of the combined data is used to estimate broadband PSFs and reconstruct the object’s spectral content. The achievable spectral resolution depends on wavelength and turbulence strength, quantified by D/r0. For λ ∼ 400 nm on a 3-m telescope, we expect R ≤ 150. We present an analysis of the speckle and spatial model and validate the simulations with on-sky images of Arcturus on a 0.7 meter telescope.

Items.Authors: Jessica B. Patel, Nurunnesa Sultana, Luis Rodriguez de Marcos, Javier G. Del Hoyo, Manuel A. Quijada, Mukti M. Rana
Items.Title: Optical and electrical properties of RF-sputtered AZO thin films for space optical applications
Items.Abstract: Transparent conductive oxides (TCOs) are of interest for optical and optoelectronic applications requiring both high optical transmission and electrical conductivity. In this work, aluminum-doped zinc oxide (AZO) thin films were deposited on glass substrates using RF magnetron sputtering under varying deposition conditions. The films were characterized using UV–Vis–NIR spectrophotometry, four-point probe electrical measurements, and surface morphology analysis to evaluate their optical transmission, sheet resistance, and surface quality. The deposited films exhibited high optical transmission at both 1064 nm and 1550 nm while maintaining measurable electrical conductivity. These results demonstrate the potential of RF-sputtered AZO thin films as transparent conductive coatings for future space optical systems requiring both high optical throughput and passive charge dissipation.

Items.Authors: Matias Marambio-Jimenez, Gabriel Olguin, Mauricio Flores, Leonardo Vanzi, Takeo Minezaki, Kentaro Motohara
Items.Title: Optical and opto-mechanical design of the TAO AIUC high resolution Y-band spectrograph front-end
Items.Abstract: The TAO AIUC High Resolution (d) Y-band Spectrograph (TARdYS) is a high-resolution (R~60000, 0.843-1.117 microns) fiber-fed instrument developed for the University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory (TAO) telescope to measure cool-star radial velocities. This paper presents the optical and opto-mechanical design of the front-end, which couples stellar light into a 50 micron (0.4'') multi-mode fiber. To minimize losses, the front-end uses a custom folded layout with commercial-off-the-shelf components and a 64-actuator deformable mirror with an integrated tip-tilt stage. Negligible differential atmospheric refraction in the Y-band justifies omitting an atmospheric dispersion corrector. Finite element analysis of the mechanical interface at the lower bent-Cassegrain focus is described. End-to-end adaptive optics simulations predict an encircled energy of 46.26% within the 0.4'' fiber core. Finally, the status of the laboratory prototype is reported.

Items.Authors: Alexis Hill, Glen Herriot, Scott Macdonald, Emma Rautio-Roe, William Thompson, Maaike van Kooten, Thushara Gunaratne, Zoran Ljusic, Brent Carlson, Ross Cheriton, Siegfried Janz, Leonid Belostotski, John Nielsen, Peter Shmerko
Items.Title: Optical aperture synthesis (OAS): lab demonstration of atmospheric turbulence correction
Items.Abstract: The Optical Aperture Synthesis (OAS) pathfinder project aims to advance adaptive optics by replacing traditional deformable mirrors and wavefront sensors with a fiber-fed integrated photonic chip capable of rapid phase control and beam combination. A laboratory demonstration shows H-band light from four fiber-fed channels combined on-chip with closed-loop phase correction, achieving an order of magnitude faster response than conventional systems. Future work will retrofit the demonstrator to a 1.2 m telescope for on-sky testing, paving the way eventually for arrays of small telescopes that may achieve micro-arcsecond resolution in near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Lorenz Wilmen, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Michael Weber, Christian Schwab, Julian Stürmer, Daniel Sablowski, Jacob Pember, Thomas Legero, David Coutts
Items.Title: Optical characterisation and modelling of a UV-Vis Fabry-Perot Etalon for wavelength calibration of EPRV spectrometers
Items.Abstract: Stable broadband Fabry–Pérot etalons are essential calibrators for extreme-precision radial-velocity (EPRV) spectrographs, providing dense, uniform reference spectra with the line symmetry, smoothness, and long-term stability required to achieve centimeter-per-second sensitivity. Such etalons must deliver high throughput and moderate finesse, while the desired stability requires fiber-coupled operation in temperature-controlled vacuum enclosures. The ultimate spectral stability and uniformity of these devices are governed by the mirror coatings, cavity substrate figure, and geometric precision, with secondary contributions from the illumination optics. We are developing a prototype broadband etalon for the U- to V-band calibration channels of the ANDES spectrometer at the ELT. In this contribution, we present high-precision metrology of the optical surfaces and compare these measurements with end-to-end simulations of the resulting etalon spectra.

Items.Authors: Nitish Singh, Sriram Sripadmanaban, Totan Chand, Juergen Schmoll, Bharat Kumar Yerra, Savitha M. S.
Items.Title: Optical design of a direct fibre-fed MO-IFS for the NLOT
Items.Abstract: Here we are presenting the initial optical design and performance analysis of a dual-channel fiber-fed Multi Object Integral Field spectrograph (MO-IFS) being developed for a future large optical telescope in India. The spectrograph is designed to directly accept an f/4 beam from a 100 µm optical fiber without additional fore-optics. The instrument consists of two optimized spectral channels covering wavelength ranges of 320–620 nm (blue channel) and 600–1000 nm (red channel). The optical design aims to achieve moderate spectral resolutions of approximately R ~ 2700 in the blue channel and R ~ 2500 in the red channel while maintaining high throughput over a broad spectral range. The spectrograph architecture includes a fiber-fed entrance slit, collimator optics, dichroic beam splitting system, dispersive elements, and dedicated camera optics for each channel. Zemax simulations were carried out to evaluate image quality, spot size distribution, spectral resolution, and detector sampling

Items.Authors: Jason R. Fucik, Richard Dekany, Jeb Bailey, Dan Reiley
Items.Title: Optical design of Z-Shooter: a broadband (20,000A) intermediate resolution high-efficiency spectrometer
Items.Abstract: An optical design for a 3-channel cross-dispersed echelle spectrometer operating from the NUV to NIR for the W.M. Keck Observatory. The spectrometer covers 20,000A in a single exposure with intermediate resolution of 20,000 for single-object spectroscopy. Designed for rapid response automated target acquisition and real-time reduction and display of acquired spectra.

Items.Authors: Charles Lee, Tyrone E. Woods, Patrick Côté, John S. Pazder
Items.Title: Optical modelling of a digital micromirror device as programmable slits for the CASTOR ultraviolet multi-object spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The Ultraviolet Multi-Object Spectrograph (UVMOS) is a proposed UV (150 to 300 nm) instrument for the CASTOR mission. The UVMOS utilizes a digital micromirror device (DMD) to create object selecting slits. The DMD consists of programmable mirrors that tilt +/- 12 degrees to selectively project the incoming field to a collecting aperture. Multi-object spectroscopy using the DMD has been demonstrated in the optical and infrared and is being evaluated for future UV missions like CASTOR and HWO. This work builds on previous simulations of a DLP7000 device in the UV using electromagnetic finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method to understand its optical performance. We introduce new results calculated from our previous simulation model that quantifies optical performance. We calculate metrics such as DMD efficiency, contrast, and effective PSF in UVMOS operating wavelengths (150 to 300 nm) to support UVMOS design.

Items.Authors: Justin Vella, Barnaby Norris, Sergio Leon-Saval, Jin Wei, Chris Betters, Andrew Ross-Adams, Adam Taras, Joss Bland-Hawthorn
Items.Title: Optimal design of application-specific photonic lanterns using Bayesian optimisation
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns (PLs) are gaining interest for focal-plane wavefront sensing and other applications, yet their design remains largely trial-and-error and heuristic-based, with little prior control of the transfer function before fabrication. Here we present a numerical optimization framework using Bayesian optimization for PL design. This enables specific, novel device properties – such as hybrid-mode-selective PLs (HMS-PLs) – to be defined and achieved using well-tested algorithms. In this example, at each iteration the algorithm tunes the physical parameters defining the PL’s central core, computes the complex transfer matrix, and compares its behaviour with the desired functionality (e.g. an ideal HMS-PL) to produce a loss value for the next iteration. The resulting optimization record also enables estimation of the underlying probability density function and visualization of parameter co-dependencies, providing a maximum-likelihood estimate for achieving hybrid-mode selectivity.

Items.Authors: Teodor Malendevych, Barnaby Norris, Christopher H. Betters, Andrew Ross-Adams, Olivier Guyon, Sergio Leon-Saval
Items.Title: Optimal single-mode injection of distorted PSFs: matched electric field optimisation using a photonic lantern
Items.Abstract: Fiber-fed astrophotonic instruments depend on coupling light into single-mode fibres (SMF). Imperfect point spread  functions (PSFs) degrade coupling efficiency due to mode field mismatch. For post-coronagraphic imaging, reduced  planet light coupling and increased stellar speckle can decrease SNR by an order of magnitude. We present a method  to actively match a multimode fibre’s (MMF) mode field to any PSF using a photonic lantern that maps the MMF  into single-mode waveguides with active phase and amplitude modulation. Operating in reverse (SMF-to-MMF),  we optimise to a predetermined mode profile using Stochastic Parallel Gradient Descent. Switching to forward  operation achieves optimal injection. Multimode interference couplers recombine science light into one SMF. We  compare simulated coupling efficiency for 3×1 lanterns versus bare SMF, demonstrate in-lab results,  and present applications to the Matched Electric Field Spectrograph for Habitable Worlds Observatory.

Items.Authors: Simon Prunet, Céline Theys, Claude Aime
Items.Title: Optimization of petal-shaped occulters for exo-Earth observation
Items.Abstract: Petal-shaped occulters are giant, formation-flying optical devices designed for use in space astronomy.     This study focuses on optimizing the shape of the occulter in order to significantly reduce Fresnel diffraction, which, in the case of a simple circular occulter, would manifest itself as an Arago spot comparable to the pupil of the telescope. Nevertheless, we will construct an occulter as the weighted sum of circular occulters such that the contribution of the complex amplitudes of the corresponding Arago spots is minimized over the telescope aperture.  This basis of circular occulters allows the use of a simple analytical form for their Fresnel diffraction. The weights are then obtained by minimizing a quadratic criterion.

Items.Authors: Julien Storm, Gert Raskin, Bart Vandenbussche, Louis Storm, Hugues Sana, Sibo Van Gool, Pierre Royer, Maddalena Reggiani, Dirk Vandepitte, Leonardo Peri, Dominic Bowman, Camille Pirat, Jorg Versluys, Mathijs Arts
Items.Title: Optomechanical design, alignment, and characterization of the CubeSpec high-resolution cross-dispersed Echelle slit spectrograph
Items.Abstract: CubeSpec is a 12U CubeSat mission designed to demonstrate high-resolution spectroscopy from a compact platform. The mission is now in construction phase with launch readiness early 2027. The payload is built around a cross-dispersed echelle spectrograph, achieving a resolving power of R≈55,000 throughout the visible wavelength range. We present here the optomechanical design, alignment, and characterization of the CubeSpec spectrograph, with a focus on validating its performance within the severe volume constraints imposed by a CubeSat platform. Characterization encompasses spectral response, which is assessed through simulations of the resolving power, order separation, wavelength coverage and a detailed analysis of the slit image.

Items.Authors: Jun W. W. Li, Kai Zhang, Zhaoying Zheng, Shun Li
Items.Title: Optomechanical structural design and dynamic performance analysis of a large-inertia fast steering mirror for astronomical image stabilization
Items.Abstract: To address image jitter in astronomical spectrometers, this paper presents the design of a large-inertia Fast Steering Mirror (FSM) carrying a 175 mm mirror (~2 kg payload). A cross-layout dual right-circular flexure hinge mechanism is proposed to ensure structural stiffness. The system is driven by four voice coil motors (VCMs) delivering a maximum continuous force of 110 N, utilizing four differential eddy current sensors for feedback. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) indicates resonant frequencies of ~100 Hz in working directions and >200 Hz in non-working directions. Experimental results confirm a maximum stroke of 1000 arcseconds and a closed-loop bandwidth of 30–40 Hz. The proposed design successfully balances high load capacity with dynamic response requirements.

Items.Authors: Justin R. Fletcher
Items.Title: Optomech: a GPU-accelerated optomechanical simulation environment for visuomotor control of hybrid optical telescopes
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets would enable unambiguous detection of the chemical signatures of exoplanetary  life. To form such an image, even for nearby planetary systems, an astronomical instrument must be sensitive to  1e−9 contrast while achieving an angular resolution on the order of 10 milliarcseconds. Fizeau optical interferometric telescopes that employ lightweight primary optical support structures may satisfy these challenging requirements at a feasible cost, but only if they are able to sustain differential motion of ~1 wave of error between the primaries. To address this optomechanical control task, we introduce and evaluate several visuomotor control approaches using a GPU-accelerated optomechanical simulation environment. We establish baseline results indicating successful closed-loop correction of differential motion, and describe several pathways for future development.

Items.Authors: Luis V. Rodriguez de Marcos, Virginia D. Wheeler, Maria G. Sales, Javier G. Del Hoyo, Mateo F. Batkis, Manuel A. Quijada, Edward J. Wollack, Scott G. Walton, David R. Boris
Items.Title: Overview of plasma-based processes for the passivation of broadband aluminum mirror coatings for UV space telescopes
Items.Abstract: Efficient and uniform Aluminum-based broadband mirrors are essential components for FUV/UV/O/IR (λ=100-2500 nm) astronomy. An ongoing collaboration between the U.S. NRL and NASA GSFC focuses on optimization of AlF3 layers grown on Al mirrors to enhance FUV/UV/O/IR performance.   In previous work we demonstrated a new process based on e-beam generated plasmas for fluorinating the surface of Al mirrors.   More recently, we have demonstrated high quality AlF3 films growth on Al mirrors through the highly conformal plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) process. This approach can lead to new coating designs.  Both processes have demonstrated high FUV/UV/O/IR reflectivity, high quality AlF3 layers, low surface roughness, good coating uniformity of the fluoride layer, low coating-induced polarization aberration, and improved durability.   This presentation shows an overview of both processes and related TRL advancement works.

Items.Authors: Benjamin Calvin, Rose Gibson, Michael Fitzgerald, Jason Fucik, Evan Kress, Ricardo Meneses, Eric Wang, Therese Cook, Chris Johnson, Jake Zimmer, Reston Nash, James Wiley, Tim Greffe, Bradley Price, Don Neill, Rishi Pahuja, Takayuki Kotani, Ashley Baker, Sam Halverson, Roger Smith, Nemanja Jovanovic, Dimitri Mawet
Items.Title: Overview of the alignment plan for the Keck/HISPEC spectrometer subsystem
Items.Abstract: The High-Resolution Infrared Spectrometer for Exoplanet Characterization (HISPEC) will use fiber-fed optics to deliver R~100,000 spectroscopy across the y, J, H, and K bands for the Keck Observatory. The science light is separated with the yJ light measured in the BSPEC spectrometer, and the HK light in the RSPEC spectrometer. The contents of these spectrometers include an initial tri-mirror anistigmat (TMA) relay to collimate science light from the fiber subsystem, reflective Germanium gratings to disperse and cross-disperse the light, and then a second TMA to bring the spectrally dispersed light to a focus at an H4RG-10 detector. In these proceedings, we present the procedure for the optical alignment of the spectrometers. We use a coordinate measuring machine to place the TMA mirrors into 3D space in accordance with our optical design and then use a Zygo interferometer to verify the double-pass optical wavefront error of each TMA relay at both warm and cryogenic temperatures.

Items.Authors: Ana Guijarro, Matthias Alter, Peter Bizenberger, María Concepción Cárdenas Vázquez, Bernhard Dorner, Matilde Fernández, Julia Gallego, Antonio J. García Segura, Jens Helmling, Armin Huber, José Miguel Ibáñez, Ulrich Mall, Richard J. Mathar, Sara Muñoz Torres, Vianak Naranjo
Items.Title: PANIC4K , from the lab to the sky: what you don't know and would like to know about this camera
Items.Abstract: PANIC4K is a wide-field near-infrared camera with a monolithic HAWAII-4RG detector for the 2.2m telescope at the Calar Alto Observatory in Spain.  In this work, the PANIC4K team (MPIA, IAA-CSIC, and CAHA) presents solutions to problems encountered with the detector performance, details the process of the non-linearity correction, and shows the capabilities and improvements of its software packages: GEIRS for the data acquisition and mechanisms control, the Observation Tool (OT) for executing observations, and the quick-look (PQL) and pipeline (PAPI) for the preliminary data processing. In addition, the team presents preliminary results from the first scientific observations carried out after commissioning, conducted by groups from several Spanish and international institutions.

Items.Authors: Jérôme Maire, Alyssa Johnson, Wei Liu, Shelley A. Wright, Aaron Brown, Benjamin Godfrey, Jamie Holder, Nikolas Korzoun, Andrew Howard, Paul Horowitz, Yuriy Popovych, Elisa Pueschel, Nicolas Rault-Wang, Sruthiranjani Ravikularaman, Dan Werthimer
Items.Title: Panoramic SETI: experimental deployment at Palomar Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Panoramic Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (PANOSETI) project is designed to detect fast optical transients spanning nanosecond-to-second timescales, including ultra-high-energy phenomena, time-domain astrophysical events, and potential technosignatures.  The deployment of multiple wide-field optical telescopes equipped with fast, synchronized detectors and separated by hundred-meter baselines enables precise parallax measurements that discriminate atmospheric Cherenkov air showers from distant astrophysical sources. Increasing the number of telescopes further improves the achievable angular resolution needed to localize the origin of gamma-ray–induced shower events.   Here we report on the first deployment and integration of a four-telescope array at Palomar Observatory. We present the technical implementation, operational strategy, and initial on-sky performance of this multi-telescope transient observatory.

Items.Authors: Alyssa Johnson, Jerome Maire, Shelley Wright, Aaron Brown, Benjamin Godfrey, Jamie Holder, Paul Horowitz, Andrew Howard, Nikolas Korzoun, Wei Liu, Yuriy Popovych, Elisa Pueschel, Nico Rault-Wang, Sruthiranjani Ravikularaman, Dan Werthimer
Items.Title: Panoramic SETI: on-sky results at Palomar Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) project is deploying wide-field optical telescopes at Palomar Observatory to search for nanosecond-scale fast transients. We present the first on-sky performance results from newly commissioned modules, including background measurements in multiple observing modes, point-source detection limits, and timing stability. We report the false-alarm rate in Pulse Height mode and demonstrate coincidence-based rejection across multiple telescopes. Early science observations targeting astrophysical point sources are described, along with initial steps toward a SETI survey. These results establish PANOSETI’s readiness for routine transient searches and technosignature observations.

Items.Authors: Frédéric J. Grandmont
Items.Title: Paradigm shift cooking in sub-meter space telescope…
Items.Abstract: While internet mega-constellations undesired impact dominate astronomy discourse, a quieter revo-lution in Earth Observation (EO) is in full motion. Feeding from the new satellite commodity echo-system, bold entrepreneurs are committed to bring space-based optical observation to the masses. Heightened international tensions also encouraging intelligence imagery independence, startups and legacy suppliers are now engaged in large-aperture high-resolution or wide-field multi-detectors tele-scope-camera systems. Using relevant project examples, we explore how modern private EO satellites could perform if pointed toward deep-space and review the compromises needed to get to the price point enabling investor’s business cases. This surge of new funding in technologies highly relevant to astronomy instrumentation is changing the space access equation. We aim to demonstrate how these advances directly benefit candidate astronomy missions such as POET, TWINKLE, and CASTOR.

Items.Authors: Kazuo Yoshioka, Ashita Yamazaki, Yusei Mitoh, Go Murakami, Yudai Suzuki, Masaki Kuwabara, Makoto Taguchi, Madoka Endo
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of optical components dedicated to Lyman-α observations from ultrasmall spacecraft
Items.Abstract: This study presents the design principles and performance evaluation of optical components optimized for hydrogen Lyman-α (121.6 nm) observations in compact ultraviolet imaging systems, including those onboard ultra-small spacecraft. UV mirrors, spectral filters, and the detector assembly were developed to achieve high reflectance, narrow-band selectivity (for separating H and D Lyman-α), and stable detection efficiency under strict constraints on size, mass, and power. Our laboratory measurements of reflectance, filter transmission, and detector response demonstrate that these components exhibit performance comparable to that of instruments used in larger-scale missions. As an application, these results are being applied to the development of the Hydrogen Imager (HI), a compact UV instrument planned for a JAXA probe participating in ESA’s Comet Interceptor mission.

Items.Authors: Taewan Kim, Yuki Moritani, Chi-Hung Yan, Shiang-Yu Wang, Jennifer Karr, Craig P. Loomis, Shitaro Koshida, Naoyuki Tamura
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of PFS fiber positioner, Cobra, using accumulated operational data
Items.Abstract: The Prime Focus Spectrograph (PFS) / Onohiula on the Subaru Telescope is a multi-object spectrograph employing 2394 robotic fiber positioners, called Cobras, to place fibers onto astronomical targets. We present a comprehensive evaluation of Cobra positioning performance and the pipelines developed for routine monitoring. The analysis focuses on three metrics: (1) convergence, which quantifies the positioning accuracy of Cobras in reaching their assigned targets; (2) geometry, which characterizes the center positions, arm lengths, and rotational ranges of Cobras; and (3) motor maps, which describe angular-dependent motor movement speeds. Using the accumulated PFS operational dataset from 2023 to 2026, we assess the long-term behavior of these metrics as functions of telescope position and operational epoch. The resulting performance trends provide essential guidance for optimizing Cobra motions during observations.

Items.Authors: Ebru UZUNÇAM, Burak Bülent Güçsav, Onur Şatır, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Performance metrics for DAG400 Telescope
Items.Abstract: The performance of 4-m class telescopes like the DAG400 Telescope depends on the coordination of optical, mechanical, thermal, and control subsystems rather than image quality alone. This work presents an integrated framework that correlates these domains using long-term observational and engineering data. Key metrics include pointing and tracking logs, image quality, PSF stability, wavefront error, tracking-error statistics, and dome- and mirror-seeing contributions, along with thermal effects. The analysis summarizes the performance criteria of such areas as optimization, such as improved control algorithms, enhanced thermal management, and possible subsystem upgrades.

Items.Authors: Stephen A. Smee, Aidan C. Gray, Stephen C. Hope, Randolph P. Hammond, Albert J. Harding, Tyson S. Hare, Leon Aslan, Robert H. Barkhouser, Christoph Birk, Julia Brady, Maren Cosens, Charlie Hull, Karim Kaismoune, Daniel D. Kelson, Gerrad Killian, Nicholas P. Konidaris, Alicia E. Lanz, Jacob McCloskey, Andrew B. Newman, Solange Ramírez, Gwen C. Rudie, William Schoenell, Jason E. Williams
Items.Title: Performance of the MIRMOS cryogenic mechanism for detector dithering and flexure compensation
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the design and cryogenic performance of a piezo-driven X-Y detector positioning stage developed for the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS). Operating at 120 K, the stage provides detector dithering and active flexure compensation to correct gravity-induced image motion as the instrument rotates at the Nasmyth focus of a 6.5 m Magellan telescope. Closed-loop position control is achieved using calibrated anisotropic magnetoresistive sensors, providing greater than 200 um of travel in both axes with submicron positioning accuracy and repeatability. The detector mount also incorporates manual tip, tilt, and focus adjustment while maintaining the thermal isolation required for 80 K detector operation. The paper describes the second-generation prototype, summarizes lessons learned from the initial design, and presents cryogenic performance measurements, including stage travel, positioning accuracy, repeatability, and sensor performance.

Items.Authors: Oliver Pineda Suárez, Jonathan Wei, Malak Galal, Melina Daniilidis, Maxime Rombach, Sébastien Pernecker, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Performance testing of a trillium-based 21-positioner module for stage-5 telescopes
Items.Abstract: Evaluating the performance metrics of theta-phi robotic positioners is crucial to gather insights into the system’s behavior and ensure their reliability during operation in Stage-5 telescopes. In this paper we present the results of the positioning performance and angular tilt tests conducted on 6.2-mm-pitch robotic positioner modules developed for high-density fiber positioning in next-generation astronomical systems. The fiber positioners from the tested prototype adopt a mechanical design based on the Trillium open design from the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) and were produced by the Japanese company Orbray. The positioners exhibited a generally acceptable performance, although noticeable anomalies affecting several metrics were identified and will require mitigation in subsequent prototypes. Nevertheless, the results indicate promising performance suitable for Stage-5 telescope instrumentation, provided that these issues are successfully resolved.

Items.Authors: Marina Centenera-Merino, Jesús Aceituno, Pedro José Amado, Miguel Andrés Sánchez-Carrasco, Javier Flores, Julius Göhring, Sergio Leon-Saval, Kalaga Madhav, Abani S. Nayak, José Luis Ortiz, David Peréz-Medialdea, Francisco José Pozuelos, Martin M. Roth, María Isabel Ruíz, Stefan Cikota, Christopher Betters, Andrew Ross-Adams
Items.Title: Photonic EMARCOT at Calar Alto: astrophotonics lab at the IAA-CSIC
Items.Abstract: The Photonic EMARCOT project introduces a scalable, modular, and cost-effective astronomical architecture. Its first phase, the MARCOT Pathfinder, is currently operating at the Calar Alto Observatory with an array of seven small telescopes designed to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio.  The system relies on advanced photonic technology developed at the IAA-CSIC Astrophotonics Lab, focusing on device fabrication, full optical characterisation, and studies of the quantum nature of light. Although high-precision equipment is now available to manufacture efficient photonic components, their optical behaviour still requires more detailed characterisation. A comprehensive protocol is therefore being developed to assess efficiency, stability, and performance. This will optimize current devices and guide the creation of future photonic architectures and quantum-technology applications.

Items.Authors: David Kappel, Martin Pertenais, Nicolas Gorius, Matthias Ammler-von Eiff, Sascha Grziwa, Demetrio Magrin, Matteo Munari, Pierre Royer, Juan Cabrera, Denis Griessbach, Thierry Appourchaux, Gonzalo Ramos, M. Teresa Rodrigo, Angel L. Valverde, Elisa Borreguero, Francisco Montoro, M. Ángeles Sierra, Lucia Espinosa, Fernando Conde, Amaia Santiago, Jesus Saiz, Lorenza Ferrari, Ann Baeke, Heike Rauer
Items.Title: PLATO camera ghosts: characterization of geometry and intensity from TVAC measurements of the flight models and the engineering model
Items.Abstract: The upcoming PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of Stars (PLATO) mission will detect and characterize exoplanets around bright stars using high-precision, long-duration photometry and stellar seismology. We analyze optical ghosts in the PLATO cameras that can contaminate photometry, using thermal-vacuum measurements on the Engineering Model and several Flight Models and compare these to optical-design simulations.

Items.Authors: Joonas Viuho, Anton N. Sørensen, Amanda A. Djupvik, Michael I. Andersen, Johan P. Fynbo, Lise B. Christensen
Items.Title: Practical experience using KDP as a thermal blocking filter
Items.Abstract: Monopotassium dihydrogen phosphate (KDP, chemical formula KH2PO4) is a material with many use cases ranging from agricultural fertilizer to a frequency modulator in near infrared lasers. One of its optical properties is high transparency from ultraviolet to 1.3µm, while being practically fully opaque at wavelengths longer than 1.8µm making it an ideal shortpass filter the near infrared. However, a few practical drawbacks exist and we will share our experiences using KDP filters at observatory conditions.

Items.Authors: Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Samattachai Tanun, Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Teerawat Kuha, Auychai Laoyang, Tarathon Intaros, Picha Ruenarrom, Manlika Pinkaew, Apichat Leckngam, Wiphu Rujopakarn
Items.Title: Precision enhancement and production-cost reduction in a multi-stage optical manufacturing workflow via CNC parameter optimization for astronomical and space systems
Items.Abstract: NARIT has developed an integrated optical-manufacturing workflow that combines CNC machining, single-point diamond turning (SPDT), and high-accuracy CMM metrology for producing mirrors, mounts, and precision opto-mechanical components for astronomical and spaceborne applications. CNC machining serves as the primary pre-processing stage, strengthened through improved CAM orientation, zero-deformation fixturing, and refined control of feed rate, cutting depth, tool engagement, and thermal-compensation strategies. These enhancements greatly improve tolerance stability, reduce rework cycles, and increase overall production efficiency. CMM measurements confirm notable gains in form error, repeatability, and dimensional stability, with clear benefits for lightweight or thin-walled components. Collectively, these advancements enable a more reliable, scalable, and cost-effective CNC–SPDT–CMM workflow to support precision optical manufacturing.

Items.Authors: Léonard Lebrun, Johannes Wüthrich, Andrin Fazan, Sean MacBride, Felipe Andrade-Oliveira, Marcelle Soares-Santos
Items.Title: Precision measurements of the axial drift in fiber positioners for spectroscopic surveys using defocus blur
Items.Abstract: Aiming for new breakthroughs in cosmology, the next-generation spectroscopic surveys will use robotic fiber positioners in the focal plane of large aperture telescopes to simultaneously observe tens of thousands of targets. To achieve this ambitious goal, the mechanical stability of the positioners is critical. In this work, we present a test setup using defocus blur to assess the stability along the optical axis of a multi-fiber positioner module, aiming for a precision of 5 micrometers, in line with the requirements of several upcoming experiments. The test is performed both on an optical table and shall in next steps be installed on a telescope mount in order to simulate the motions expected for an actual astronomical instrument. This defocus test setup may be used for characterization of prototypes during the R&D phase as well as for quality control during the production phase, ensuring that axial drifts in the positioners remain within the survey requirements.

Items.Authors: Pieter Vuylsteke, Bart Vandenbussche, Wim De Meester, Kwinten Missiaen, Jesus Perez Padilla, Gert Raskin, Wim Pessemier, Johan Morren, Saskia Prins, Jacob Pember, Kaustubh Hakim, Alexis Brandeker, Christian Schwab, Manuel Güdel, Benjamin Montet, Denis Defrère, Hans Van Winckel
Items.Title: Precision photometry with the MARVEL telescope array
Items.Abstract: MARVEL is a new facility intended for precision Doppler spectroscopy. The four robotic 0.8m telescopes have been installed in 2025. We have commissioned a precision photometry mode to commence early science observations, while the facilities Echelle spectrometer is being assembled. Here we report on operation of the facility, the implementation of the photometry capability, and results achieved so far.

Items.Authors: Jinghua Mao
Items.Title: Pre-launch calibration of the ultraviolet imager (UVI) for the SMILE Mission
Items.Abstract: This paper conducts comprehensive multi-dimensional ground calibration on the Ultraviolet Imager (UVI) of the Sino-European joint SMILE satellite, verifies its qualified radiometric and geometric performance, and the established calibration system provides technical references for similar aurora detection payloads.

Items.Authors: Varun Shah, Vincenzo Cotroneo, Jose Antonio Dieste, Alejandro P. Marques, Maria Hernandez, Gil Moretto
Items.Title: Progress of thermal-forming of normal-incidence glass optics for the LiveMirror project
Items.Abstract: Thermal-forming of glass optics is the process of slumping thin glass sheets onto a mold using a suitable thermal cycle. This is a cost-effective process to fabricate high-performing light mirrors from readily available materials. The ‘EIC Live-Mirror’ project aims to produce lightweight, thermally-formed mirrors that are actively supported by electro-active polymer-based actuators. We perform slumping tests on stainless steel mandrels and analyze the figure and surface roughness of the produced samples to optimize the thermal-forming process, constrain the transfer of spatial frequencies, and ascertain what parameters introduce specific errors to guide the overall slumping process and the mandrel manufacturing requirements for larger optics.

Items.Authors: Thomas Schneider, Myung Cho, Gary Poczulp, Logan Sato, Il Kweon Moon, Youra Jun
Items.Title: Progress on a new M2 for the Gemini North telescope to minimize mechanical support print-through effects
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Observatory is procuring a new secondary mirror (M2) for the Gemini North telescope to improve image quality by minimizing print-through deformations. The M2 was replaced in 2008, but the root cause of the print-through was not properly addressed and was actually worsened. The current M2 at Gemini North suffers from approximately ± 1µm of surface deformation, resulting in an approximate 20% reduction in Strehl ratio. Finite element analysis(FEA) of the M2 and its support system has identified the root cause of the print-through. By making several changes to the mechanical supports, FEA has shown that the surface deformation can be reduced to approximately ±25nm or less. This paper details the root cause of the print-through effects and the design changes that will be made to the new M2 mechanical supports that will remediate them in the new M2. The current progress of the M2 fabrication is also detailed.

Items.Authors: Changhui Rao, Youming Guo, Lanqiang Zhang, Xuejun Rao, Hua Bao, Xinlong Fan, Libo Zhong, Zibo Ke, Lingxiao Li, Wenru Li, Nanfei Yan, Qianhan Zhou, Xiaoying Gong
Items.Title: Progress on astronomical adaptive optics in NLAO, China
Items.Abstract: This presentation reports recent progress by China’s National Laboratory of Adaptive Optics (NLAO), established in 2024. In night-time astronomy, we are developing key AO systems: an AO/GLAO system with a 930mm deformable secondary mirror and four sodium laser guide stars (Na LGS) for a 4.2m telescope, and a Nasmyth AO system with cascade DMs for a 14.5m telescope. The Na LGS technology was successfully tested on-sky in 2025. For solar observation, the 1.8m Chinese Large Solar Telescope (CLST) with a 457-element AO system is completed and scheduled for installation in 2027. An AO/GLAO system for a 2.5m solar telescope has completed indoor testing. New systems for prominence observation and MCAO upgrade are also underway. We are further developing a 60cm compact solar adaptive telescope for high-contrast imaging.

Items.Authors: Thomas Schneider, Cristian Moreno, Tomislav Vucina, Clayton Ah Hee, Claudio Araya
Items.Title: Progress on creating a durable UV-enhanced silver coating for the Gemini Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Observatory has been searching for a UV-enhanced silver coating that can be applied to the primary, secondary, and tertiary mirror that will allow for faster observations out to 350nm. The coating must allow for at least 80% reflectivity at 350nm without compromising reflectivity and emissivity in near-infrared wavelengths. The coating must survive for at minimum of 5 years between coatings without significant degradation from environmental stressors or in-situ washes. The coating must be able to be stripped with acids that are no more toxic than the current chemical stripping agents. The UV-enhanced coating must be able to produced with the 3 magnetrons that are mounted in the Gemini chamber. This paper reports on the successes, partial successes, failures and potential new paths forwards for producing a durable UV-enhanced silver coating for astronomical observatories.

Items.Authors: Ross C. McCurdy, Drew M. Miles, Jake A. McCoy, Fabien Grise, Randall L. McEntaffer
Items.Title: Progress updates on blazed UV grating development with electron-beam lithography and TASTE
Items.Abstract: High performance UV reflection gratings are an essential technology for enabling key science objectives for HWO and potential future observatories in the coming decade. In recent years, funded NASA studies have developed electron-beam lithography (EBL) to write custom variable-line-space groove layouts. We will present on results of the development and optimization of EBL and the TASTE process to fabricate blazed UV gratings over a range of line densities and blaze angles. Specifically, we will discuss results from exploring the nanofabrication parameter space for UV grating fabrication with EBL and TASTE, limitations that we have encountered, and plans for fabricating larger format gratings at different periods and blaze angles for experimental testing and performance verification.

Items.Authors: Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Barnaby Norris, Christopher H. Betters, Julia J. Bryant, Laird M. Close, Daniel S. Dahl, Olivier Guyon, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Sergio Leon-Saval, Nathan K. Long, Jared R. Males, Andrew Ross-Adams
Items.Title: PWI-SPEC: an optical, multi-resolution spectrograph optimised for high fibre-count astrophotonic wavefront sensing and imaging instruments
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonic instruments have seen a recent surge of interest, including photonic integrated circuits and photonic lantern wavefront sensors and imagers. Their advancement, however, requires measurement of an ever-growing number of SM outputs, with specific spectral and temporal sampling demands, necessitating a spectrograph design dissimilar to current general purpose astronomical spectrographs. PWI-SPEC is an optical spectrograph being built at Astralis-USyd and SAIL for the Photonic Wavefront Imager (PWI) module of the MagAO-X extreme adaptive optics system, purpose-designed to accept 100s of SMFs by using a unique rotated 2D fibre matrix array, and offer both lower- and higher-resolution modes tailored to wavefront sensing and imaging respectively. The final spectra are imaged at optimal pixel sampling and separation onto an Andor CB2 sCMOS camera which allows 100 SMFs at low spectral resolution (R=136) to be read out at ~1000 frames per second, with 1.4 electrons read noise.

Items.Authors: Rui Zhang, Zhen Zhang, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Quantifying centroid shifts induced by glass in the GFA of JUST
Items.Abstract: The traditional star alignment methods mostly use spot projection to achieve the coordinate conversion between the focal plane fiber and the guide star camera (GFA). However, the guide star camera of the JUST Spectroscopic Telescope adopts a double-layer glass encapsulation structure. This special design introduces systematic errors caused by the glass-optical interface into the traditional star alignment method, and the deviation of the glass installation collimation will further affect the systematic error of the traditional calibration method. To quantify the above-mentioned errors, this thesis conducts an experiment on the extraction accuracy of the spot center for mask holes. By collecting spot images with or without glass, the spot center of gravity is extracted using the light center of gravity algorithm, and the absolute error of the Euclidean distance of spots with the same number is used as the measurement index for the offset of the spot center of gravity.

Items.Authors: Tara R. Crowe, Miguel Romer, Ameer Batarseh, Stephen Eikenberry, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Daniel Cruz-Delgado, Stephanos Yerolatsitis, Miguel Bandres, Sergio Leon-Saval, Kerri Donaldson Hanna, Robert Conwell, Matthew Cooper, Caleb Dobias, Genevieve Markees, Christina Moraitis, David Smith, Aiden Akers, Vincent Miller, Sarah Thibaut, Nathen Nguyen
Items.Title: Quantum-Inspired Imaging (QI2) through atmospheric turbulence: on-sky results
Items.Abstract: Modal-basis imaging techniques facilitated by photonic lanterns (PLs) offer a unique method of focal-plane (FP) wavefront estimation. For large telescopes, atmospheric turbulence induces perturbations in the phase of a wavefront and is the most significant cause of image quality/resolution degradation. We demonstrate our PL-based wavefront sensor (WFS) to measure and correct wavefront fluctuations with use of prior adaptive optics (AO) correction. By leveraging the wavelength sensitivity of PLs, our approach allows us to deduce turbulent phase variations over a broad wavelength range and break the degeneracy between atmospheric turbulence and diffraction, the latter of which is taken to be the fundamental resolution limit of traditional imaging systems. We present the design and on-sky results of our PQI2-850 quantum-inspired imaging system and demonstrate our approach's efficacy for PL-WFS in the non-linear regime and with high-order wavefront aberrations.

Items.Authors: Gavin Leroy, Juan Paolo Lorenzo Gerardo Barrios, Maximilian von Wietersheim-Kramsta, Richard Massey, Richard G. Hayes, Jacob A. Kegerreis, David Lagattuta, Zane D. Lentz, James W. Nightingale, Jesper Skottfelt, Felix Vecchi
Items.Title: Radiation damage to the Hubble Space Telescope has been several years out of phase with the Solar cycle
Items.Abstract: As well as obtaining beautiful images of the Universe, the Hubble Space Telescope's CCD detectors are sensitive radiation dosimeters that have been in Low Earth Orbit for more than 24 years. The rate of radiation damage they received has varied over each Solar cycle, but several years out of phase with the appearance of sunspots or coronal mass ejections. We investigate functions of time that successfully fit the damage to telescopes elsewhere in the Solar system. We obtain accurate fits to Hubble data but with physically absurd parameter values. During image post-processing, such fits can be used empirically, to correct more than 99.5% of the radiation damage's effect on image quality. Our results highlight the diversity of radiation environments in different parts of our Solar system, and the complexity of Low Earth Orbit in particular. Our results also motivate continued monitoring of radiation damage to current spacecraft, to more reliably predict the lifespan of future missions.

Items.Authors: Remya B. S., Sriram Sripadmanabhan
Items.Title: Realuminization of 1 m Carl Zeiss telescope mirror and reflectivity degradation studies at Vainu Bappu Observatory
Items.Abstract: The 1-m Carl Zeiss Ritchey–Chrétien telescope at the Vainu Bappu Observatory (VBO), Kavalur, underwent full re-aluminization using the calibrated 60-inch high-vacuum coating chamber. The old coating was chemically stripped and the mirror cleaned before aluminium deposition by thermal evaporation under ~10⁻⁶ mbar after ion-beam cleaning. The 36-filament firing unit ensured uniform vaporization. Witness samples showed a coating thickness of ~1210 Å (±100 Å) and ~90% reflectivity (365–970 nm) with <2% non-uniformity. Adhesion and pinhole tests confirmed coating integrity. The Cassegrain and Coudé mirrors achieved 88–89% reflectivity. Post-installation monitoring showed reflectivity declining from 90% to 75.4% over one year.

Items.Authors: Emily van Hese, Niek Doelman
Items.Title: Receiver diversity technology for satellite to ground low-loss free space optical communication
Items.Abstract: Free space optical communication promises high-data rate and high-security data links. Efficient ground station receiver design that mitigates atmospheric turbulence link losses is necessary to achieve this. Photonic technologies including few-mode fibres, adaptive optics to maintain optimal spot size and location in the receiver, and receiver diversity with multiple smaller apertures can each reduce atmospheric link losses. In this work, a numerical study is performed of these methods for a satellite-to-ground link in the presence of atmospheric phase and amplitude aberrations. Statistical analysis of instantaneous free-space to fibre coupling shows the changing distribution of coupled power under each mitigation method and under hybrid systems. The possibility and performance of combined solutions are presented.
